subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard represent human-approval/action-required cards as a built-in UI concept, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave that state to existing status and labels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: the fix could be UI-local, metadata/label-driven, or a new plugin config surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
options.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention count or card affordance without creating plugin config yet.

options.title: Add configurable prominent labels
options.body: Define a plugin-owned config contract for approval-needed labels with docs and tests for the new user-visible config surface.

options.title: Keep labels and blocked status only
options.body: Defer first-class human-action UX and document the existing blocked/status/filter workflow as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
recommendation.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention count or card affordance without creating plugin config yet.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the Workboard plugin and dashboard surface and is the strongest history-backed owner for the product-surface choice.
